gloss: to grow older; to age; to accumulate years

definitions.gloss: to grow older; to age; to accumulate years
definitions.explanation: To advance in age over time. A softer, more dignified way to express aging than direct words like 'to get old.' Often carries a positive or neutral nuance of gaining experience and maturity.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねるごとに{味|あじ}が{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: With each passing year, more character emerges.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねても{元気|げんき}でいたい。
examples.english: I want to stay healthy even as I grow older.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねて{初|はじ}めて{分|わ}かることがたくさんある。
examples.english: There are many things you can only understand after growing older.

notes:
Literally 'to pile up years.' A euphemistic and respectful way to describe aging. The verb {重|かさ}ねる (to pile up, to accumulate) emphasizes the gradual accumulation of years and experience.

USAGE:
Preferred over {老|ふ}ける (to age, to grow old) or {年|とし}を{取|と}る (to get older) in polite contexts because it avoids negative connotations. Often used in reflective or philosophical contexts about life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねるごとに: with each passing year
- {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねても: even as one ages
- {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねた{人|ひと}: an older person (respectful)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {年|とし}を{取|と}る: to get older — more neutral, everyday expression
- {老|ふ}ける: to age, to grow old — can sound negative
- {歳月|さいげつ}を{経|へ}る: for years to pass — more literary
